column1: # What each pattern compiles to: its elements in order (a run of one kind as
# L(n)), its chains, and the form of its graph NFA, or `literal`. These pin
# the engine routing, where a slower path would still answer right; both
# runtimes read this file (Glob::shape, SegmentMatcher.shape).
# Format: SHAPE<TAB>PATTERN[<TAB>PATTERN...] (several patterns: one union).
# Keep NFA rows within 32 states or past 170: JS keeps 32 in an int32 and
# steps the rest sparsely; Rust keeps 64 in a u64 and 170 in dense rows (4 KiB).
# A union member with several `**` keeps an NFA of its own up to 64 states in
# Rust and 32 in JS; past that the graph NFA takes the whole union.
literal
L W:affix | chains 1 | nfa none
L G0 W:affix | chains 1 | nfa none
G0 W:set | chains 1 | nfa none
G0 W:affix | chains 1 | nfa none
L G0 W:nfa | chains 1 | nfa none
L G0 W:set(2) | chains 1 | nfa none
W:index | chains 1 | nfa none
W:set G0 W:affix | chains 1 | nfa none
G0 L G0 L | chains 0 | nfa small
W:set G0 L G0 W:affix(2) | chains 2 | nfa small
# Members that differ only in the literal ending one segment merge into a
# set there; a literal member, or one that starts its segment, stays as it
# is.
G0 W:set G1 W:affix | chains 2 | nfa small
L G0(2) W:set W:affix | chains 2 | nfa small
L(5) | chains 3 | nfa small
L(4) G1 | chains 2 | nfa small
L W:set G1 L G0 W:affix | chains 2 | nfa small
G0 L G0 W:set L | chains 2 | nfa small
L W:affix L W:affix W:set L G1 | chains 2 | nfa small
G0 L G0 W:affix(2) L | chains 3 | nfa small
L G0 L G0 L G0(2) L G0 L G0 L G0 W:set W:affix W:set W:affix L W:affix(4) | chains 9 | nfa small
L(7) | chains 8 | nfa small
G0 W:nfa | chains 1 | nfa none
L(200) | chains 0 | nfa sparse
L(4000) | chains 0 | nfa sparse
L G1 | chains 1 | nfa none
G0 | chains 1 | nfa none
L G0 W:set | chains 1 | nfa none
W:nfa | chains 1 | nfa none
W:nfa | chains 1 | nfa none
G0 L G1 | chains 0 | nfa small
L(4) W:nfa | chains 2 | nfa small
